claim: The eukaryotic replisome assembles around the CMG helicase.
source: The eukaryotic replisome assembles around the CMG helicase, which stably associates with DNA replication forks throughout elongation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about replisome structure.

claim: CMG stably associates with DNA replication forks throughout elongation.
source: The eukaryotic replisome assembles around the CMG helicase, which stably associates with DNA replication forks throughout elongation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact.

claim: When replication terminates, CMG is ubiquitylated on its Mcm7 subunit.
source: When replication terminates, CMG is ubiquitylated on its Mcm7 subunit and disassembled by the Cdc48/p97 ATPase.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact from prior work.

claim: CMG is disassembled by the Cdc48/p97 ATPase after ubiquitylation.
source: When replication terminates, CMG is ubiquitylated on its Mcm7 subunit and disassembled by the Cdc48/p97 ATPase.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact.

claim: Ubiquitylation of CMG is tightly repressed throughout elongation by the Y-shaped DNA structure of replication forks.
source: By reconstituting these processes with purified budding yeast proteins, we show that ubiquitylation is tightly repressed throughout elongation by the Y-shaped DNA structure of replication forks.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the reconstitution experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: Termination removes the repressive DNA structure that blocks CMG ubiquitylation.
source: Termination removes the repressive DNA structure, whereupon long K48-linked ubiquitin chains are conjugated to CMG-Mcm7, dependent on multiple replisome components that bind to the ubiquitin ligase SCFDia2.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the reconstitution experiments.

claim: Long K48-linked ubiquitin chains are conjugated to CMG-Mcm7 after termination removes the repressive DNA structure.
source: Termination removes the repressive DNA structure, whereupon long K48-linked ubiquitin chains are conjugated to CMG-Mcm7, dependent on multiple replisome components that bind to the ubiquitin ligase SCFDia2.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the reconstitution experiments.

claim: CMG ubiquitylation is dependent on multiple replisome components that bind to the ubiquitin ligase SCFDia2.
source: Termination removes the repressive DNA structure, whereupon long K48-linked ubiquitin chains are conjugated to CMG-Mcm7, dependent on multiple replisome components that bind to the ubiquitin ligase SCFDia2.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the reconstitution experiments.

claim: The mechanism of CMG ubiquitylation pushes CMG beyond a '5-ubiquitin threshold' that is inherent to Cdc48.
source: This mechanism pushes CMG beyond a '5-ubiquitin threshold' that is inherent to Cdc48, which specifically unfolds ubiquitylated Mcm7 and thereby disassembles CMG.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the reconstitution experiments.

claim: Cdc48 specifically unfolds ubiquitylated Mcm7 to disassemble CMG.
source: This mechanism pushes CMG beyond a '5-ubiquitin threshold' that is inherent to Cdc48, which specifically unfolds ubiquitylated Mcm7 and thereby disassembles CMG.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the reconstitution experiments.

claim: Eukaryotic chromosomes are duplicated just once per cell cycle by the replisome.
source: Eukaryotic chromosomes are duplicated just once per cell cycle, by a large molecular machine called the replisome (Bell and Labib, 2016; Burgers and Kunkel, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Replisome assembly is initiated in the G1-phase of the cell cycle.
source: Replisome assembly is initiated in the G1-phase of the cell cycle, when the six Mcm2-7 ATPases are loaded around double strand DNA (dsDNA) at origins of replication, as a 'head-to-head' double hexamer (Evrin et al., 2009; Li et al., 2015; Remus et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The six Mcm2-7 ATPases are loaded around double strand DNA at origins of replication as a 'head-to-head' double hexamer.
source: Replisome assembly is initiated in the G1-phase of the cell cycle, when the six Mcm2-7 ATPases are loaded around double strand DNA (dsDNA) at origins of replication, as a 'head-to-head' double hexamer (Evrin et al., 2009; Li et al., 2015; Remus et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Each Mcm2-7 hexamer comprises a two-tiered ring, which represents the catalytic core of the helicase.
source: Each Mcm2-7 hexamer comprises a two-tiered ring, which represents the catalytic core of the helicase that subsequently unwinds the DNA duplex at replication forks (Aparicio et al., 1997; Ishimi, 1997; Labib et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Origin unwinding cannot occur until S-phase.
source: Origin unwinding cannot occur until S-phase, when two protein kinases induce multiple 'firing factors' to recruit the remaining helicase subunits known as Cdc45 and the GINS complex.
evidence: This is established knowledge about cell cycle regulation of DNA replication.

claim: Two protein kinases induce multiple 'firing factors' to recruit Cdc45 and the GINS complex in S-phase.
source: Origin unwinding cannot occur until S-phase, when two protein kinases induce multiple 'firing factors' to recruit the remaining helicase subunits known as Cdc45 and the GINS complex.
evidence: This is established knowledge about cell cycle regulation of DNA replication.

claim: The association of Mcm2-7 with Cdc45 and GINS splits the Mcm2-7 double hexamer into two CMG helicase complexes.
source: The association of Mcm2-7 with Cdc45 and GINS splits the Mcm2-7 double hexamer into two CMG (Cdc45-Mcm2-7-GINS) helicase complexes (Abid Ali et al., 2016; Douglas et al., 2018; Moyer et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: CMG assembly is coupled to initial origin melting.
source: CMG assembly is coupled to initial origin melting (Douglas et al., 2018), so that each of the two nascent CMG helicases is associated with around 6–7 bp of unwound single-strand DNA (ssDNA).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Each nascent CMG helicase is associated with around 6–7 bp of unwound single-strand DNA.
source: CMG assembly is coupled to initial origin melting (Douglas et al., 2018), so that each of the two nascent CMG helicases is associated with around 6–7 bp of unwound single-strand DNA (ssDNA).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The transient opening of a gate in CMG leads to complete exclusion of the lagging strand DNA template from the Mcm2-7 central channel.
source: Finally, the transient opening of a poorly defined 'gate' in CMG leads to complete exclusion of the lagging strand DNA template from the Mcm2-7 central channel (Wasserman et al., 2019), in a step that requires the Mcm10 protein (Douglas et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Exclusion of the lagging strand DNA template from the Mcm2-7 central channel requires the Mcm10 protein.
source: Finally, the transient opening of a poorly defined 'gate' in CMG leads to complete exclusion of the lagging strand DNA template from the Mcm2-7 central channel (Wasserman et al., 2019), in a step that requires the Mcm10 protein (Douglas et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: CMG encircles the template of the leading strand during DNA synthesis.
source: Multiple factors associate with the two helicases to form two replisomes (Gambus et al., 2006; Sengupta et al., 2013), leading to the initiation of DNA synthesis at a pair of bidirectional replication forks, with CMG encircling the template of the leading strand.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The association of CMG with replication fork DNA is uninterrupted from initiation to termination.
source: The association of CMG with replication fork DNA is uninterrupted from initiation to termination, based on the stable entrapment of the leading strand DNA template in the central channel of Mcm2-7.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about CMG structure and function.

claim: Displacement of CMG from DNA blocks fork progression irreversibly.
source: This is important, because displacement of CMG from DNA blocks fork progression irreversibly (Labib et al., 2000), since CMG cannot be reassembled at a replication fork during S-phase.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: CMG cannot be reassembled at a replication fork during S-phase.
source: This is important, because displacement of CMG from DNA blocks fork progression irreversibly (Labib et al., 2000), since CMG cannot be reassembled at a replication fork during S-phase.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about CMG assembly.

claim: The convergence of two replication forks leads very quickly to CMG disassembly and replisome dissolution.
source: Nonetheless, the convergence of two replication forks leads very quickly to CMG disassembly and replisome dissolution (Dewar and Walter, 2017; Gambus, 2017), which is likely to represent the final stage of DNA replication termination.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: CMG unloading occurs after the formation of a fully ligated DNA product during plasmid replication in Xenopus laevis egg extracts.
source: Consistent with this view, CMG unloading occurs after the formation of a fully ligated DNA product during plasmid replication in Xenopus laevis egg extracts (Dewar et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Complete plasmid replication and formation of covalently closed products occurs in a reconstituted yeast replication system that lacks the components required for CMG disassembly.
source: Moreover, we observed complete plasmid replication and the formation of covalently closed products, using a reconstituted yeast replication system that lacks the components required for CMG disassembly (Deegan et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: Post-termination CMG complexes must encircle dsDNA after DNA synthesis has been completed.
source: This indicated that post-termination CMG complexes must encircle dsDNA, after DNA synthesis has been completed.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that replication completes without CMG disassembly.

claim: The key regulated step during replisome disassembly is the ubiquitylation of the Mcm7 subunit of CMG.
source: The key regulated step during replisome disassembly is the ubiquitylation of the Mcm7 subunit of CMG (Maric et al., 2014; Moreno et al., 2014), which in budding yeast is mediated by the cullin ubiquitin ligase known as SCFDia2 and the ubiquitin conjugating enzyme Cdc34 (Maric et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: In budding yeast, CMG-Mcm7 ubiquitylation is mediated by the cullin ubiquitin ligase SCFDia2 and the ubiquitin conjugating enzyme Cdc34.
source: The key regulated step during replisome disassembly is the ubiquitylation of the Mcm7 subunit of CMG (Maric et al., 2014; Moreno et al., 2014), which in budding yeast is mediated by the cullin ubiquitin ligase known as SCFDia2 and the ubiquitin conjugating enzyme Cdc34 (Maric et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: CMG-Mcm7 ubiquitylation was not observed when converging replication forks stalled in the absence of Pif1.
source: In the absence of Pif1, converging replication forks stalled to produce a 'late replication intermediate' (Figure 1B, lane 2). Under these conditions, CMG-Mcm7 ubiquitylation was not observed (Figure 1C, lane 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 1B-C.

claim: Mcm7 ubiquitylation was readily detected in reactions containing Pif1 that supported DNA replication termination.
source: However, Mcm7 ubiquitylation was readily detected in reactions containing Pif1 (Figure 1C, lane 1), which supported DNA replication termination and the production of fully replicated 3.2 kb plasmids (Figure 1B, lane 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 1B-C.

claim: Mcm7 ubiquitylation was dependent upon Pif1 helicase activity.
source: Moreover, Mcm7 ubiquitylation was dependent upon Pif1 helicase activity (Figure 1D (ii), compare lanes 2 and 3; Pif1-K264A lacks helicase activity and cannot support DNA replication termination).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: CMG ubiquitylation is tightly blocked before DNA replication termination in the reconstituted replication system, without requiring a deubiquitylase enzyme.
source: These findings indicated that CMG ubiquitylation is tightly blocked before DNA replication termination in the reconstituted replication system, without requiring a deubiquitylase enzyme to counteract SCFDia2 and the ubiquitin conjugation system.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data showing no ubiquitylation before termination.

claim: CMG-Mcm7 ubiquitylation is induced when converging replication forks undergo DNA replication termination, without needing the action of any additional factors other than the E1, E2 and E3 ubiquitylation enzymes.
source: The data also demonstrate that CMG-Mcm7 ubiquitylation is induced when converging replication forks undergo DNA replication termination, without needing the action of any additional factors other than the E1, E2 and E3 ubiquitylation enzymes.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data showing ubiquitylation occurs with just E1, E2, and E3.

claim: CMG ubiquitylation is blocked in the reconstituted in vitro replication system when replication initiates in the absence of Mcm10.
source: Correspondingly, CMG ubiquitylation is blocked in the reconstituted in vitro replication system, when replication initiates in the absence of Mcm10 (Figure 1E (i), compare lanes 1–2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Both nascent CMG and post-termination CMG were ubiquitylated to an equivalent degree upon release from DNA.
source: Remarkably, both nascent CMG and post-termination CMG were ubiquitylated to an equivalent degree upon release from DNA (Figure 1E (i), compare lanes 3–4; the efficiency of DNase digestion is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The regulation of CMG ubiquitylation during chromosome duplication is not based on an activating signal that can only occur during DNA replication termination at a pair of converged forks.
source: These findings strongly indicate that the regulation of CMG ubiquitylation during chromosome duplication is not based on an activating signal that can only occur during DNA replication termination at a pair of converged forks.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data showing nascent CMG can be ubiquitylated when released from DNA.

claim: Nascent CMG is potentially a substrate for SCFDia2, but ubiquitylation is blocked during initiation, dependent upon the DNA structure of the origin.
source: Instead, nascent CMG is potentially a substrate for SCFDia2, but ubiquitylation is blocked during initiation, dependent upon the DNA structure of the origin.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data showing nascent CMG can be ubiquitylated when released from DNA.

claim: CMG released from pre-termination forks was ubiquitylated just as efficiently as CMG derived from fully replicated plasmid DNA.
source: Strikingly, CMG released from pre-termination forks (Figure 1E (ii), lane 3, -Pif1) was ubiquitylated just as efficiently as CMG derived from fully replicated plasmid DNA (Figure 1E (ii), lane 4, +Pif1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The regulation of CMG ubiquitylation during chromosome replication is based on DNA-dependent repression during initiation and elongation, which is then relieved during DNA replication termination.
source: Overall, therefore, these data indicate that the regulation of CMG ubiquitylation during chromosome replication is based on DNA-dependent repression during initiation and elongation, which is then relieved during DNA replication termination.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data showing CMG can be ubiquitylated when released from DNA at any stage.

claim: Even 1 nM of SCFDia2 was sufficient to ensure that 15 nM CMG was ubiquitylated with extremely high efficiency in the presence of other replisome factors.
source: Strikingly, even 1 nM of SCFDia2 was sufficient to ensure that 15 nM CMG was ubiquitylated with extremely high efficiency in the presence of other replisome factors (Figure 2B, right half; Figure 2—figure supplement 1A shows that the reaction was dependent upon addition of E1, E2 and E3).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The ubiquitylation reaction was highly selective for CMG-Mcm7.
source: The reaction was highly selective for CMG-Mcm7 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B–C) and involved the conjugation of long K48-linked ubiquitin chains onto more than one lysine of Mcm7 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, right panel).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The ubiquitylation reaction involved the conjugation of long K48-linked ubiquitin chains onto more than one lysine of Mcm7.
source: The reaction was highly selective for CMG-Mcm7 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B–C) and involved the conjugation of long K48-linked ubiquitin chains onto more than one lysine of Mcm7 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, right panel).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Ubiquitylation of Ctf4 and Mrc1 was undetectable at 1 nM SCFDia2.
source: In contrast, ubiquitylation of the previously reported substrates Ctf4 and Mrc1 (Mimura et al., 2009) was undetectable at 1 nM SCFDia2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D), and instead required concentrations of SCFDia2 that are saturating for CMG ubiquitylation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: SCFDia2 ubiquitylates CMG-Mcm7 with remarkable efficiency and selectivity, without any requirement for CMG to have passed through the steps of DNA replication termination.
source: Overall, these findings demonstrated that SCFDia2 ubiquitylates CMG-Mcm7 with remarkable efficiency and selectivity, without any requirement for CMG to have passed through the steps of DNA replication termination.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data showing efficient ubiquitylation of recombinant CMG.

claim: CMG ubiquitylation does not require the presence of dsDNA in the central channel of Mcm2-7.
source: Moreover, these data show that CMG ubiquitylation does not require the presence of dsDNA in the central channel of Mcm2-7, or the encounter of CMG with the rear face of PCNA from a converged replication fork.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data showing efficient ubiquitylation of recombinant CMG without DNA.

claim: CMG ubiquitylation does not require the encounter of CMG with the rear face of PCNA from a converged replication fork.
source: Moreover, these data show that CMG ubiquitylation does not require the presence of dsDNA in the central channel of Mcm2-7, or the encounter of CMG with the rear face of PCNA from a converged replication fork.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data showing efficient ubiquitylation of recombinant CMG without DNA.

claim: CMG-Mcm7 ubiquitylation was markedly impaired by an excess of fork DNA containing a short 5' flap that corresponded to the excluded DNA strand.
source: Compared to reactions lacking DNA (Figure 2C (ii), lane 1), CMG-Mcm7 ubiquitylation was markedly impaired by an excess of fork DNA containing a short 5' flap that corresponded to the excluded DNA strand (Figure 2C (ii), lanes 2–3).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The inhibitory effect of fork DNA was observed over a broad range of E3 concentrations.
source: Moreover, the inhibitory effect of fork DNA was observed over a broad range of E3 concentrations (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: CMG ubiquitylation was not inhibited by an otherwise identical DNA substrate that lacked the excluded DNA strand.
source: CMG ubiquitylation was not inhibited by an otherwise identical DNA substrate that lacked the excluded DNA strand (Figure 2C (ii), lane 4).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: ssDNA versions of either strand did not impair CMG ubiquitylation.
source: Moreover, ssDNA versions of either strand did not impair CMG ubiquitylation (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The Y-shaped DNA structure of a replication fork inhibits the ability of SCFDia2 and Cdc34 to support CMG ubiquitylation.
source: These findings indicated that the Y-shaped DNA structure of a replication fork inhibits the ability of SCFDia2 and Cdc34 to support CMG ubiquitylation.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data showing fork DNA inhibits ubiquitylation.

claim: Ctf4 ubiquitylation was detectable in the presence of 10 nM E3 ligase and was independent of CMG.
source: As noted above, Ctf4 is a much less efficient substrate of SCFDia2 than CMG (Figure 2D, compare Ctf4 and Mcm7), but Ctf4 ubiquitylation was detectable in the presence of 10 nM E3 ligase and was independent of CMG (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Ctf4 ubiquitylation was not affected by the presence of fork DNA, in contrast to ubiquitylation of CMG-Mcm7.
source: Notably, Ctf4 ubiquitylation under these conditions was not affected by the presence of fork DNA, in contrast to ubiquitylation of CMG-Mcm7 (Figures 2D and 10 nM [E3]).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 2D and 2F.

claim: Forked DNA is not a generic inhibitor of SCFDia2.
source: These findings demonstrate that forked DNA is not a generic inhibitor of SCFDia2, and instead indicate that ubiquitylation of CMG-Mcm7 is specifically impaired by its association with a replication fork, dependent upon the presence of the excluded DNA strand.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data showing differential effects of fork DNA on CMG vs Ctf4 ubiquitylation.

claim: Ubiquitylation of CMG-Mcm7 is specifically impaired by its association with a replication fork, dependent upon the presence of the excluded DNA strand.
source: These findings demonstrate that forked DNA is not a generic inhibitor of SCFDia2, and instead indicate that ubiquitylation of CMG-Mcm7 is specifically impaired by its association with a replication fork, dependent upon the presence of the excluded DNA strand.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data showing fork DNA inhibits CMG ubiquitylation.

claim: SCFDia2 was unable to ubiquitylate Mcm7 in reactions in which CMG was replaced by free Cdc45, Mcm2-7 and GINS.
source: SCFDia2 was unable to ubiquitylate Mcm7 in reactions in which CMG was replaced by free Cdc45, Mcm2-7 and GINS (Figure 3A, compare lanes 1–2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Mcm7 ubiquitylation can only take place in the context of the CMG helicase.
source: Therefore, Mcm7 ubiquitylation can only take place in the context of the CMG helicase, thereby explaining why Mcm7 ubiquitylation is restricted to S-phase (Maric et al., 2014) and cannot occur in the context of Mcm2-7 double hexamers or unloaded Mcm2-7 complexes.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data showing only assembled CMG can be ubiquitylated.

claim: CMG-Mcm7 ubiquitylation was almost entirely dependent upon the presence of other replisome components.
source: Moreover, CMG-Mcm7 ubiquitylation was almost entirely dependent upon the presence of other replisome components (Figure 3A, lane 3), indicating that the preferred substrate of SCFDia2 is Mcm7 in the context of the CMG-replisome.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The preferred substrate of SCFDia2 is Mcm7 in the context of the CMG-replisome.
source: Moreover, CMG-Mcm7 ubiquitylation was almost entirely dependent upon the presence of other replisome components (Figure 3A, lane 3), indicating that the preferred substrate of SCFDia2 is Mcm7 in the context of the CMG-replisome.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data showing replisome components enhance ubiquitylation.

claim: The high efficiency of CMG ubiquitylation was influenced by three specific components of the replisome: Pol ε, Mrc1 and Ctf4.
source: Subsequently, a series of dropout experiments indicated that the high efficiency of CMG ubiquitylation was influenced by three specific components of the replisome, namely Pol ε, Mrc1 and Ctf4 (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: CMG-Mcm7 ubiquitylation in the presence of just Pol ε, Mrc1 and Ctf4 was equivalent to reactions containing the complete set of replisome components.
source: Moreover, CMG-Mcm7 ubiquitylation in the presence of just these three replisome components was equivalent to reactions containing the complete set (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: CMG-Mcm7 ubiquitylation was dramatically impaired in the absence of Ctf4.
source: CMG-Mcm7 ubiquitylation was dramatically impaired in the absence of Ctf4, and ubiquitin chains were substantially shorter in the absence of Mrc1, whereas dropout of Pol ε had a milder effect (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Ubiquitin chains were substantially shorter in the absence of Mrc1.
source: CMG-Mcm7 ubiquitylation was dramatically impaired in the absence of Ctf4, and ubiquitin chains were substantially shorter in the absence of Mrc1, whereas dropout of Pol ε had a milder effect (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Removal of Pol ε had no impact on CMG ubiquitylation in the absence of Mrc1.
source: Moreover, removal of Pol ε had no impact on CMG ubiquitylation in the absence of Mrc1 (Figure 3C, left panel), with which it interacts (Lou et al., 2008), suggesting that Pol ε contributes indirectly to CMG ubiquitylation by helping to recruit Mrc1 to the helicase.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Pol ε contributes indirectly to CMG ubiquitylation by helping to recruit Mrc1 to the helicase.
source: Moreover, removal of Pol ε had no impact on CMG ubiquitylation in the absence of Mrc1 (Figure 3C, left panel), with which it interacts (Lou et al., 2008), suggesting that Pol ε contributes indirectly to CMG ubiquitylation by helping to recruit Mrc1 to the helicase.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data and prior knowledge about Pol ε-Mrc1 interaction.

claim: Mrc1 and Ctf4 made additive contributions to CMG ubiquitylation.
source: In contrast, Mrc1 and Ctf4 made additive contributions to CMG ubiquitylation (Figure 3C, right panel), and residual CMG ubiquitylation in the absence of both factors was equivalent to reactions containing CMG alone (compare Figure 3C, right panel with Figure 3A, left panel).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Mrc1 and Ctf4 were important for efficient CMG ubiquitylation during termination in the reconstituted DNA replication system.
source: Importantly, we confirmed that Mrc1 and Ctf4 were important for efficient CMG ubiquitylation during termination in the reconstituted DNA replication system (Figure 3D – ubiquitylation was monitored under conditions where plasmid replication was complete, despite the absence of Mrc1 and Ctf4).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Pol ε, Mrc1 and Ctf4 each contributed to recruitment of SCFDia2 to the CMG helicase.
source: Subsequently, we found that Pol ε, Mrc1 and Ctf4 each contributed to recruitment of SCFDia2 to the CMG helicase (Figure 3E, which shows association of the Cdc53 cullin subunit of SCFDia2 with CMG), to an extent that reflected their contribution to CMG-Mcm7 ubiquitylation (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 3E-F.

claim: The recruitment of SCFDia2 to CMG by Mrc1 and Ctf4 likely reflects the direct binding of Mrc1 and Ctf4 to the amino-terminal domain of tetratricopeptide repeats (TPR) in Dia2.
source: These data likely reflect the direct binding of Mrc1 and Ctf4 to the amino-terminal domain of tetratricopeptide repeats (TPR) in Dia2 (Mimura et al., 2009; Morohashi et al., 2009; Mukherjee and Labib, 2019).
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data combined with prior knowledge from citations.

claim: The inherently high efficiency of CMG ubiquitylation by SCFDia2 reflects a complicated targeting mechanism for the E3 ligase, whereby the replisome components Ctf4 and Mrc1 contribute additively to the recruitment of SCFDia2 to CMG.
source: In summary, therefore, the inherently high efficiency of CMG ubiquitylation by SCFDia2 reflects a complicated targeting mechanism for the E3 ligase, whereby the replisome components Ctf4 and Mrc1 contribute additively to the recruitment of SCFDia2 to CMG.
evidence: This is a summary inference from the experimental data.

claim: Replisome tethering of SCFDia2 predisposes the reaction towards the production of long K48-linked chains on CMG-Mcm7.
source: In addition, however, replisome tethering of SCFDia2 also predisposes the reaction towards the production of long K48-linked chains on CMG-Mcm7 (Figures 1–3).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figures 1-3.

claim: In the absence of Ctf4 and Mrc1, not only is CMG ubiquitylated less frequently, but the attached chains are shorter.
source: In the absence of Ctf4 and Mrc1, therefore, not only is CMG ubiquitylated less frequently, but the attached chains are shorter (Figure 3B–C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 3B-C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Ubiquitylated CMG was disassembled with extremely high efficiency, dependent upon Cdc48, Ufd1-Npl4 and ubiquitylation.
source: In this way, we observed that ubiquitylated CMG was disassembled with extremely high efficiency, dependent upon Cdc48, Ufd1-Npl4 and ubiquitylation (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: CMG disassembly was inefficient when the helicase was ubiquitylated in the absence of Mrc1 and Ctf4.
source: However, CMG disassembly was inefficient when the helicase was ubiquitylated in the absence of Mrc1 and Ctf4 (Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Despite the absence of Ctf4, Mrc1 and SCFDia2 in the final step, ubiquitylated CMG was still disassembled very efficiently by Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4.
source: Despite the absence of Ctf4, Mrc1 and SCFDia2 in the final step, ubiquitylated CMG was still disassembled very efficiently by Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4 (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Mrc1 and Ctf4 promote CMG disassembly by stimulating the formation of long ubiquitin chains on CMG-Mcm7, but are not required subsequently for the action of Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4.
source: These findings indicated that Mrc1 and Ctf4 promote CMG disassembly by stimulating the formation of long ubiquitin chains on CMG-Mcm7, but are not required subsequently for the action of Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data showing efficient disassembly after removal of Mrc1 and Ctf4.

claim: Stable binding of Cdc48-E588A-Ufd1-Npl4 to ubiquitylated CMG was dependent upon the conjugation of very long polyubiquitin chains to Mcm7.
source: Surprisingly, stable binding of Cdc48-E588A_Ufd1-Npl4 to ubiquitylated CMG was dependent upon the conjugation of very long polyubiquitin chains to Mcm7 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), despite previous studies showing that Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4 can bind with varying affinity to monomeric substrates that are conjugated to three or more ubiquitins (Bodnar and Rapoport, 2017), or at least six ubiquitins (Tsuchiya et al., 2017).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Long ubiquitin chains increase the stability of binding to Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4.
source: These findings indicate that long ubiquitin chains increase the stability of binding to Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4, but the data do not address what length of ubiquitin chain is functionally required for a substrate to be unfolded by Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data showing binding depends on chain length.

claim: Mcm7 with 1–4 ubiquitins was largely retained on the beads throughout the reaction, indicating that CMG disassembly was blocked.
source: As shown in Figure 4G, Mcm7 with 1–4 ubiquitins was largely retained on the beads throughout the reaction, indicating that CMG disassembly was blocked.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Mcm7 with 5–7 ubiquitins was partially released into the supernatant.
source: In contrast, Mcm7 with 5–7 ubiquitins was partially released into the supernatant (Figure 4G, left side), whereas longer ubiquitin chains on Mcm7 led to rapid dissociation from CMG (Figure 4G, right side, 10 nM E2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Longer ubiquitin chains on Mcm7 led to rapid dissociation from CMG.
source: In contrast, Mcm7 with 5–7 ubiquitins was partially released into the supernatant (Figure 4G, left side), whereas longer ubiquitin chains on Mcm7 led to rapid dissociation from CMG (Figure 4G, right side, 10 nM E2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: CMG disassembly is gated by a 'ubiquitin threshold' that controls the action of Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4.
source: These findings indicated that CMG disassembly is gated by a 'ubiquitin threshold' that controls the action of Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4, analogous to an equivalent threshold that is thought to control the degradation of proteasomal substrates (Swatek and Komander, 2016).
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data showing chain length requirements.

claim: Conjugation of at least five ubiquitins to Mcm7 is required for CMG disassembly.
source: Conjugation of at least five ubiquitins to Mcm7 is required for CMG disassembly, although we note that longer ubiquitin chains increase the efficiency of disassembly still further (consistent with the binding data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Longer ubiquitin chains increase the efficiency of CMG disassembly beyond the 5-ubiquitin threshold.
source: Conjugation of at least five ubiquitins to Mcm7 is required for CMG disassembly, although we note that longer ubiquitin chains increase the efficiency of disassembly still further (consistent with the binding data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data.

claim: The replisome components Mrc1 and Ctf4 ensure that SCFDia2 pushes CMG above a ubiquitin threshold that governs the action of Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4.
source: In summary, therefore, the replisome components Mrc1 and Ctf4 ensure that SCFDia2 pushes CMG above a ubiquitin threshold that governs the action of Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4.
evidence: This is a summary inference from the experimental data.

claim: The concerted recruitment mechanism for the E3 ligase guarantees that CMG disassembly is highly efficient during DNA replication termination, once the inhibitory effect of DNA replication fork structure has been removed.
source: In this way, the concerted recruitment mechanism for the E3 ligase guarantees that CMG disassembly is highly efficient during DNA replication termination, once the inhibitory effect of DNA replication fork structure has been removed.
evidence: This is a summary inference from the experimental data.

claim: CMG disassembly disrupts the association of Mcm2-7 with Cdc45 and the 4-protein GINS complex, but GINS remains intact and can still interact with Cdc45 to some degree.
source: We found that CMG disassembly disrupts the association of Mcm2-7 with Cdc45 and the 4-protein GINS complex, but GINS remains intact and can still interact with Cdc45 to some degree (Figure 5A, lanes 1–4).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Ubiquitylated Mcm7 no longer associated with the other 10 CMG subunits after helicase disassembly and instead was bound to Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4.
source: Strikingly, ubiquitylated Mcm7 no longer associated with the other 10 CMG subunits after helicase disassembly and instead was bound to Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4 (Figure 5A, lanes 5–6), uniquely amongst the 11 subunits of CMG (Figures 5A and 7–8).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The Cdc48-FtsH fusion protein supported efficient disassembly of ubiquitylated CMG helicase.
source: The Cdc48-FtsH fusion protein supported efficient disassembly of ubiquitylated CMG helicase (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), leading to the production of degraded fragments of ubiquitylated Mcm7 (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Degradation of Mcm7 by Cdc48-FtsH was dependent on Ufd1-Npl4 and ATP.
source: This was dependent not only on Ufd1-Npl4 and ATP (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B), but also upon the physical connection of Cdc48 to FtsH (Figure 5C, compare lanes 2–3).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Degradation of Mcm7 by Cdc48-FtsH was dependent upon the physical connection of Cdc48 to FtsH.
source: This was dependent not only on Ufd1-Npl4 and ATP (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B), but also upon the physical connection of Cdc48 to FtsH (Figure 5C, compare lanes 2–3).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The other 10 subunits of CMG were not degraded by Cdc48-FtsH, except for a very small amount of Mcm4.
source: In contrast, the other 10 subunits of CMG were not degraded by Cdc48-FtsH (Figure 5D), except for a very small amount of Mcm4 that correlated with the low level of Mcm4 ubiquitylation in the reconstituted system (Figure 5D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B–E, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B; note that Mcm4 is adjacent to Mcm7 within the structure of the CMG helicase).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4 disassembles ubiquitylated CMG by specifically unfolding the ubiquitylated subunit (almost exclusively Mcm7), which is translocated through the central pore of Cdc48.
source: These findings demonstrated that Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4 disassembles ubiquitylated CMG by specifically unfolding the ubiquitylated subunit (almost exclusively Mcm7), which is translocated through the central pore of Cdc48.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data showing selective degradation of Mcm7.

claim: Unfolding of ubiquitylated Mcm7 induces the irreversible collapse of the CMG helicase complex.
source: This then induces the irreversible collapse of the CMG helicase complex.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data showing CMG disassembly upon Mcm7 unfolding.

claim: The ubiquitylated Mcm7 subunit of CMG remains associated with Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4 after helicase disassembly.
source: As noted above, the ubiquitylated Mcm7 subunit of CMG remains associated with Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4 after helicase disassembly (Figure 5A, lanes 7–8).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Partial cleavage of the remaining ubiquitin chains with the Cdc48-linked deubiquitylase Otu1 led to release of unfolded Mcm7 from Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4.
source: As observed previously for ubiquitylated GFP (Bodnar and Rapoport, 2017), partial cleavage of the remaining ubiquitin chains with the Cdc48-linked deubiquitylase Otu1 (Ernst et al., 2009; Stein et al., 2014) led to release of unfolded Mcm7 from Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C–D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C-D.

claim: The data in this study are inconsistent with all of the previously suggested models for the regulation of CMG ubiquitylation during DNA replication termination.
source: As discussed above and summarised in Figure 6—figure supplement 1, the data in this study are inconsistent with all of the previously suggested models for the regulation of CMG ubiquitylation during DNA replication termination.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the experimental data contradicting prior models.

claim: Ubiquitylation of the CMG-replisome is inherently efficient from the moment of CMG assembly onwards.
source: Based on our data, we instead propose a new model (Figure 6; Figure 6—figure supplement 1), whereby ubiquitylation of the CMG-replisome is inherently efficient from the moment of CMG assembly onwards, but ubiquitylation is inhibited throughout elongation by the DNA structure of a replication fork.
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the experimental data.

claim: The only role of DNA replication termination is to remove the Y-shaped DNA structure of a fork, thereby exposing CMG to ubiquitylation by SCFDia2 and Cdc34.
source: According to the new model, the only role of DNA replication termination is to remove the Y-shaped DNA structure of a fork, thereby exposing CMG to ubiquitylation by SCFDia2 and Cdc34.
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the experimental data.

claim: The commitment to ubiquitylation occurs when the last bp of parental dsDNA is unwound, and the repressive fork DNA structure is removed from CMG.
source: Whilst it is likely that CMG encounters the 5' end of the opposing fork's lagging strand and moves onto dsDNA in the few minutes before CMG is disassembled (Dewar et al., 2015), the model indicates that the commitment to ubiquitylation occurs when the last bp of parental dsDNA is unwound, and the repressive fork DNA structure is removed from CMG.
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the experimental data.

claim: CMG will be ubiquitylated and disassembled via the same mechanism whenever replication terminates by a single fork arriving at a telomere or a nick in the leading strand DNA template.
source: Notably, the model also predicts that CMG will be ubiquitylated and disassembled via the same mechanism, whenever replication terminates by a single fork arriving at a telomere or a nick in the leading strand DNA template (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a prediction from the proposed model.

claim: The ubiquitylation of soluble CMG likely represents a physiologically important process that is responsible for disassembling the 32 CMG helicases that are released from the ends of 16 chromosomes in a haploid budding yeast cell.
source: For this reason, the ubiquitylation of soluble CMG (Figures 2–3) likely represents a physiologically important process that is responsible for disassembling the 32 CMG helicases that are released from the ends of 16 chromosomes in a haploid budding yeast cell, thereby explaining why CMG is not detected after the completion of S-phase (Gambus et al., 2006).
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data and prior observations.

claim: The parental DNA strand that is excluded from the Mcm2-7 channel of CMG sterically inhibits the ubiquitylation of CMG-Mcm7.
source: We propose that the parental DNA strand that is excluded from the Mcm2-7 channel of CMG, corresponding to the template of the lagging strand at replication forks, sterically inhibits the ubiquitylation of CMG-Mcm7.
evidence: This is a mechanistic proposal based on the experimental data.

claim: The N-terminal domain of Mcm7 contains a preferred site for ubiquitylation by SCFDia2 and Cdc34.
source: Consistent with this view, the N-terminal domain of Mcm7 contains a preferred site for ubiquitylation by SCFDia2 and Cdc34 (Figure 4E and Maric et al., 2017), together with a hairpin that functions as a 'separation pin' to split the two parental DNA strands (Baretic et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and citations.

claim: The N-terminal domain of Mcm7 contains a hairpin that functions as a 'separation pin' to split the two parental DNA strands.
source: Consistent with this view, the N-terminal domain of Mcm7 contains a preferred site for ubiquitylation by SCFDia2 and Cdc34 (Figure 4E and Maric et al., 2017), together with a hairpin that functions as a 'separation pin' to split the two parental DNA strands (Baretic et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: Replication fork DNA specifically inhibits CMG-Mcm7 ubiquitylation, without affecting the ubiquitylation of other replisome components such as Ctf4.
source: Moreover, replication fork DNA specifically inhibits CMG-Mcm7 ubiquitylation, without affecting the (less efficient) ubiquitylation of other replisome components such as Ctf4 (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The C-terminal Leucine-Rich Repeats (LRR) of Dia2 are required for SCFDia2 association with the replisome.
source: In this regard, we note that the C-terminal Leucine-Rich Repeats (LRR) of Dia2, which comprise the canonical substrate-binding domain, (Cardozo and Pagano, 2004; Willems et al., 2004), are also required for SCFDia2 association with the replisome (Mukherjee and Labib, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: CMG-Mcm7 is the preferred substrate of SCFDia2.
source: Given that CMG-Mcm7 is the preferred substrate of SCFDia2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B–E), we predict that the Dia2-LRR binds directly to CMG.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data and is used to make a prediction.

claim: CMG is still a target for SCFDia2 in the absence of other replisome components or the Dia2-TPR, albeit with much reduced efficiency.
source: Consistent with this view, CMG is still a target for SCFDia2 in the absence of other replisome components (Figure 3A) or the Dia2-TPR (Maculins et al., 2015), albeit with much reduced efficiency.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data and supported by a citation.

claim: SCFDia2 co-purified with the yeast replisome after DNase treatment of S-phase cell extracts.
source: In this regard, we note that previous work showed that SCFDia2 co-purified with the yeast replisome after DNase treatment of S-phase cell extracts (Morohashi et al., 2009), which would have removed the inhibitory effect of the excluded DNA strand.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Ubiquitylation of nascent CMG is inhibited during initiation in the reconstituted DNA replication system, consistent with in vivo observations in yeast cells lacking Mcm10.
source: Ubiquitylation of nascent CMG is inhibited during initiation in the reconstituted DNA replication system (Figure 1D–E), consistent with in vivo observations in yeast cells lacking Mcm10 (Kanke et al., 2012; van Deursen et al., 2012; Watase et al., 2012).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data and supported by citations.

claim: The functional requirement of Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4 for long ubiquitin chains provides a form of quality control.
source: We propose two consequences of this mechanism for the biology of the CMG helicase. Firstly, the requirement for long ubiquitin chains provides a form of quality control. Unscheduled ubiquitylation events during elongation are likely to be inefficient and should thus only produce short chains, which would not trigger premature CMG disassembly by Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4.
evidence: This is a proposed consequence based on the experimental findings.

claim: The functional requirement of Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4 for long ubiquitin chains has driven the evolution of pathways that exploit short-chain ubiquitylation of CMG during elongation for other uses.
source: Secondly, the functional requirement of Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4 for long ubiquitin chains has driven the evolution of pathways that exploit short-chain ubiquitylation of CMG during elongation for other uses.
evidence: This is a proposed evolutionary consequence based on the experimental findings.

claim: The TRAIP ubiquitin ligase leads to slow ubiquitylation of CMG at inter-strand DNA crosslinks, initially favoring the recruitment of DNA repair factors such as the NEIL3 glycosylase to short poly-ubiquitin chains.
source: For example, work with Xenopus egg extracts indicates that the TRAIP ubiquitin ligase leads to slow ubiquitylation of CMG at inter-strand DNA crosslinks, initially favoring the recruitment of DNA repair factors such as the NEIL3 glycosylase to short poly-ubiquitin chains (Wu et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Short-chain ubiquitylation of CMG does not trigger premature CMG disassembly.
source: Our data show why such short-chain ubiquitylation does not trigger premature CMG disassembly.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data showing the 5-ubiquitin threshold.

claim: The mechanism by which Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4 disassembles ubiquitylated CMG involves specific unfolding of the ubiquitylated Mcm7 subunit.
source: Our data demonstrate that the mechanism by which Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4 disassembles ubiquitylated CMG involves specific unfolding of the ubiquitylated Mcm7 subunit (Figure 6, step 3), probably initiated by unfolding of a ubiquitin component of the K48-linked ubiquitin chain that is attached to Mcm7 (Twomey et al., 2019).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental data and supported by a citation.

claim: GINS and Cdc45 are segregated from the remainder of the Mcm2-7 proteins during CMG disassembly.
source: In this way, GINS and Cdc45 are segregated from the remainder of the Mcm2-7 proteins.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data showing selective unfolding of Mcm7.

claim: Unfolded Mcm7 is likely degraded by the proteasome after release from Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4.
source: It is likely that unfolded Mcm7 is then degraded by the proteasome, either directly due to the persistence of an oligo-ubiquitin chain on Mcm7 after release from Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4, or else via cellular pathways for the ubiquitylation and degradation of misfolded proteins (Enam et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a speculation based on the experimental findings and supported by a citation.

claim: Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4 exclusively unfolds the ubiquitylated subunit(s) of a protein complex.
source: Although other adaptors of Cdc48/p97 can recruit the ATPase to unfold non-ubiquitylated protomers of a protein complex, as is the case for an inhibitor of protein phosphatase 1 (Weith et al., 2018), our data indicate that Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4 exclusively unfolds the ubiquitylated subunit(s) of a protein complex.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data showing selective unfolding of ubiquitylated Mcm7.

claim: The ubiquitin ligases that control CMG helicase disassembly during DNA replication termination have diverged widely during the course of eukaryotic evolution.
source: Finally, we note that the ubiquitin ligases that control CMG helicase disassembly during DNA replication termination have diverged widely during the course of eukaryotic evolution.
evidence: This is established knowledge about evolutionary divergence.

claim: Yeasts utilise SCFDia2 for CMG helicase disassembly.
source: Although yeasts utilise SCFDia2 (Maculins et al., 2015; Morohashi et al., 2009), metazoa employ an unrelated cullin ligase called CUL2LRR1 (Dewar et al., 2017; Sonneville et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Metazoa employ an unrelated cullin ligase called CUL2LRR1 for CMG helicase disassembly.
source: Although yeasts utilise SCFDia2 (Maculins et al., 2015; Morohashi et al., 2009), metazoa employ an unrelated cullin ligase called CUL2LRR1 (Dewar et al., 2017; Sonneville et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The manner by which the CMG helicase embraces its DNA template is likely to be very similar in all eukaryotic species.
source: Nevertheless, the manner by which the CMG helicase embraces its DNA template is likely to be very similar in all eukaryotic species.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about CMG structure conservation.
